extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, respondents in USPTO disciplinary proceedings, and Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards governing interim suspension of a practitioner from practice before the USPTO, including grounds for suspension, notice/service requirements, timelines for responses, referral to a hearing officer, publication and notification duties, and post-suspension compliance/reinstatement obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for interim suspension (serious crime/ethical violations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interim suspension pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.25(b) may be ordered for violation of the ethical standards set out in 37 C.F.R. §§ 10.23(a), 10.23(b)(3), and 10.23(b)(4); the request for interim suspension was predicated upon proof that Respondent committed a serious crime (conviction of two counts of felony prescription fraud, Va. Code § 18.2-258.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office relied on a certified copy of a sentencing order showing conviction(s) as the proof supporting suspension. The order states the interim suspension was appropriate given those convictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and notice requirements for Notice and Order
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order was mailed first class certified mail, return receipt requested, to the most recent address provided by Respondent pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.11 and to a street address where the OED Director reasonably believed Respondent received mail; if mailed notices are returned, service by publication pursuant to 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.25(b)(2) and 11.35(b) may be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The mailing to one address was returned 'Undeliverable as Addressed' and to the other 'MOVED LEFT NO ADDRESS - UNABLE TO FORWARD,' and the OED published service by notice in the Official Gazette (dates given). Use of certified mail and publication in the Official Gazette follow the cited regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent's opportunity to file a response to the Notice and Order
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order directed Respondent to file, within 40 days, a response containing information sufficient to establish a genuine issue of material fact based upon any grounds permissible under 37 C.F.R. § 11.25(b)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to file a timely response may result in a determination that there is no genuine issue of material fact and that interim suspension and referral for formal proceedings are appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of no genuine issue of material fact and effect
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director demonstrates the predicates for interim suspension and Respondent does not establish a genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.25(b), it is appropriate to order interim suspension and refer the Complaint to a hearing officer for a formal disciplinary proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order determines both (1) there is no genuine issue of material fact pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.25(b) and (2) interim suspension and referral are appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral to hearing officer and filing an answer to the Complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: The Complaint shall be referred to a hearing officer in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.25(b)(5) for formal disciplinary proceedings; Respondent must file a written answer to the Complaint in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.36 with the hearing officer within thirty (30) days from the date of the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order provides the hearing officer's mailing and hand-delivery addresses. The Order also requires Respondent to serve a copy of his answer on the OED Director by mail to the specified USPTO address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of answer on OED Director (address and method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within thirty (30) days from the date of the Final Order, Respondent shall serve a copy of his answer to the Complaint on the OED Director by mail to: Mail Stop 8, Office of the Solicitor, United States Patent and Trademark Office, P.O. Box 1450, Alexandria, Virginia 22313-1450.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order specifies both the address and that service must be by mail; filing with the hearing officer and service on OED Director are separate obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content and publication of Notice of Interim Suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: OED Director is ordered to publish in the Official Gazette a Notice of Interim Suspension that identifies the practitioner (name, location, registration number), states the interim suspension pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.25, describes the criminal conviction (counts and statutory citation), conviction date, alleged factual basis (e.g., altering prescriptions), sentence details, and cites the statutory and regulatory provisions under which the action is taken (35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.25 and 11.59).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order includes the specific text published in the Official Gazette and notes that disciplinary decisions are posted at the OED Reading Room URL.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification duties of OED Director to governmental and state authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall give notice of the Final Order to (1) appropriate employees of the USPTO; (2) interested departments, agencies, and courts of the United States; and (3) appropriate authorities of any State in which Respondent is known to be a member of the bar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This directs broad intergovernmental notification in addition to publication in the Official Gazette.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of interim suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended on an interim basis from the practice of patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the USPTO in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.25(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The suspension covers all categories of practice before the USPTO (patent, trademark, and other non-patent law) for the interim period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent's obligations during suspension and for reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is ordered to comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58; Respondent must comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.25(e) should Respondent seek reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order explicitly mandates compliance with the cited regulatory provisions concerning duties upon suspension and the procedure/requirements to seek reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of certified court documents as proof for disciplinary action
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director relied upon a certified copy of a March 17, 2009, Sentencing Order from Commonwealth of Virginia v. Dean James Tricarico showing convictions as the factual predicate for the Complaint and the request for interim suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certified court records demonstrating conviction may serve as sufficient proof to support interim suspension proceedings under the cited regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where disciplinary decisions are posted (public access)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary decisions regarding practitioners are posted at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room electronically located at the provided URL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order cites the OED Reading Room (URL) as the place where such decisions are available to the public.
